name: SOL Late-Confirmed Reversal
description: Right after a 15-minute SOL window opens, if the previous window moved a lot (more than 1.5 of its usual standard deviations) and its last 5 minutes also ran hard the same way, buy the side that bets on a reversal. Bursts that run into the 15-minute boundary tend to give some back in the next window, but the Kalshi SOL price at the open treats the window as a coin flip.
hypothesis: Same mechanism as eth-midrev, moved to SOL with the ETH rule unchanged (L=300 s, |z15|>1.5, |z5|>1.5 same sign, first 1.5 min, mid 30-70c): the burst into a 15-minute boundary (candle-close traders, hedgers of 15-minute binaries) overshoots and reverses, and the thinner KXSOL15M opening quote ignores it even more than ETH's does. Losers: opening takers/quoters pricing the window as a coin flip. Wrong if: the full walk-forward isn't positive with CI > 0 and >=60% of months positive, May-Aug is flat or negative (the decay eth-overreact saw), the 2x-latency run loses, or the lockbox loses.
next: Paper ~2 weeks (~1.5 trades/day) to check fills at the open on SOL's thinner books (slip_c=1). Lockbox was a weak pass (+2.1c, CI -7.3..+10.8; Sep -1.0c), so judge paper on fills, not PnL. Then kalshi-lab audit sol-midrev and the user's OK for a live trial.
